answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity post a refundable bond that only unlocks after it completes a full epoch of peer-graded work. One real agent pays it once, but N fake identities cost N times the bond, so the attacker funds every head they spawn. Duplicate clusters found by peers are slashed in full, and detection turns a hollow profit into a real loss. Spamming therefore becomes a voyage that must cross a whole epoch before paying out, while the honest lagoon grows as forfeited bonds flow to real participants.
